text:
For pair production γγ → e⁺e⁻, the threshold condition in a head-on collision is:

$$s = (2m_e c^2)^2$$

The invariant s for two photons with energies E (high energy γ) and ε (CMB photon) colliding head-on is:

$$s = 2E\varepsilon(1-\cos\theta)$$

For head-on collision (θ = 180°):

$$s = 4E\varepsilon$$

Setting this equal to threshold:

$$4E\varepsilon = 4(m_e c^2)^2$$

$$E = \frac{(m_e c^2)^2}{\varepsilon}$$

Plugging in values:
- $m_e c^2 = 0.511 \text{ MeV} = 0.511 \times 10^6 \text{ eV}$
- $\varepsilon = 10^{-3} \text{ eV}$

$$E = \frac{(0.511 \times 10^6)^2}{10^{-3}} \text{ eV}$$

$$E = \frac{0.2611 \times 10^{12}}{10^{-3}} \text{ eV} = 0.2611 \times 10^{15} \text{ eV}$$

$$E = 2.61 \times 10^{14} \text{ eV} = 2.61 \times 10^{5} \text{ GeV}$$

This matches option (B).

Answer: B
